# Authoring an Egatari lesson with a chat AI

English | [日本語](authoring-with-llms.ja.md)

For a free chat AI, choose the light instructions in the editor’s “New” and copy them; they are a lighter version.

**For people.** This is an instruction pack for chat AIs (claude.ai, Gemini, ChatGPT, …) that writes a first draft of an [Egatari](https://github.com/egatari/egatari-spec) lesson (Egatari is an open file format; Egatari Studio is the editor): HTML slides with step-by-step reveals and a spoken script. No install and no coding tool needed.

1. Open a new chat and paste **everything from “Instructions for the AI” to the end**, followed by the part set packs you need (below), and end with the **What I want** section filled in (title, audience, length, language, speakers, other wishes; one narrator by default). The editor assembles the pack from your answers to a few questions and copies it, with “What I want” at the end (**New… → answer the four questions → Copy the instructions**; it puts what you wrote at the end, so you can send it even when the chat turns the long paste into an attachment).
2. The AI’s output has two grey boxes (code blocks). Copy each with the copy button at its top right, paste them into the two fields of step 5 of that dialog in Egatari Studio (slides and script), and press **Create** (if you copied the whole output, paste it into either field and it is split in two). The editor gives every slide a stable id, runs the quality check and opens it.
3. Fix the findings of the quality check, or press **Copy a fix request for your AI** in the quality check panel and paste that into the same chat; paste the AI’s output in step 3 of **Revise…** and press **Replace**. To add slides later, use **Insert slide… → Have a chat AI write it**.

**Paste it each time, or register it once.** Pasting the pack at the start of each chat works in every chat AI and always uses the current pack; this is the default. If you write lessons often, you can keep the pack in the chat AI instead (copy it from the editor, or save this file and the part set packs you need as text files):

- **claude.ai**: make a Project and put the pack in its instructions, or add it as a project file; every chat in the project uses it. Where skills are available, a skill can carry the pack too.
- **ChatGPT**: a Project (instructions or files), or a custom GPT. The pack is longer than a custom GPT's instruction box allows, so upload it as a Knowledge file and write “Follow the attached Egatari instruction pack exactly” in the instructions.
- **Gemini**: a Gem; put the pack in its instructions, or add it as a file if it is too long.

A registered pack does not update itself. Its first lines say **Pack version: …**; after the editor is updated, compare that with a freshly copied pack and replace the registered one when they differ. The make skill (`plugins/egatari/skills/make/`) is generated from the same source. It writes the two files; the separate studio skill (`skills/studio/`) guides local quality checks, builds and adding audio.

This file and the part set packs together are the **full pack**: the standards, the output format and every standard and specialized part (extra parts, used only for very particular material, are never in the pack). This file always describes the standard parts. Each **part set pack** adds the specialized parts of one kind of material: [stats](llm-parts/stats.md) (`m-boxplot`, `m-heatmap`, `m-hist`, `m-seq`); [data](llm-parts/data.md) (`m-balance`, `m-ci`, `m-code`, `m-folds`, `m-mapping`, `m-sampling`); [math](llm-parts/math.md) (`m-hissan`, `m-numberline`, `m-sweep`, `m-tape`); [maps](llm-parts/maps.md) (`m-map-japan`, `m-map-world`); [kokugo](llm-parts/kokugo.md) (`m-gendai`, `m-kanbun`, `m-kobun`); [english](llm-parts/english.md) (`m-syntax`); [music](llm-parts/music.md) (`m-keyboard`, `m-score`); [business](llm-parts/business.md) (`m-market`); [tools](llm-parts/tools.md) (`m-timer`); [science](llm-parts/science.md) (`m-orbit`, `m-particles`). The editor's New… copies the standard parts and the sets of the parts ticked in its parts list; in the light instructions, the standard parts other than the four core ones get only their one-line catalogue entry, so that every standard part fits the light instructions' limit: 45 KB and 31,000 for the paste length (UTF-16 code units plus line feeds, about where Gemini cuts a paste), whichever is reached first. `node kit/llm-pack.mjs --sets stats,math --lang en` prints the light instructions with those sets; add `--plan paid` to describe every part in full, and `--sets all --plan paid` for the full pack. Sizes (KB = UTF-8 bytes / 1024; paste length = UTF-16 code units + line feeds, since a paste may arrive with CRLF):

The Expert/Novice dialogue of R-dialogue (written only when asked for) follows the cognitive-apprenticeship design of [arXiv:2607.12235](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12235) (implementation and prompts: <https://github.com/moiku/gemini-tts-lecture-generation>).

# Instructions for the AI

Pack version: `303b7661`

You will write one short **Egatari lesson**: HTML slides with step-by-step reveals (`deck.html`) and a spoken script for it (`narration.md`). Both files are built and quality-checked automatically; anything not described here is not available. Write the lesson in the language the user asks for (slides and script in the same language). Standards have ids such as **R-fit**; a fix request names the standards a draft broke. The user's request is in **What I want** at the end (or in the conversation before it): choose sensibly for any field that is empty or missing, and if both A and B are left, follow the one with content.

**Before you start (the most common failures):**

- **Both code blocks must be complete and closed.** Never stop in the middle of a block (R-output). Without an outline, keep the lesson short (5–8 slides). When the request gives an outline and a range of its slides, write exactly the slides of that range: the editor asks for at most 6 at a time, so they fit.
- **Sizes on the 1280×720 slide** (the quality checker measures them, R-fit): the body area is 1184 × 443 px (to 565 px; 1184 × 558 with `noconcl`). Body text is 32 px with 46 px per line, so about **8 lines** fit; every overflowing 46 px is one line to cut. **All text, also inside figures and parts, is at least 24 px.**
- **Charts and figures:** parts draw their labels at 24–28 px whatever their size (their SVG uses their own pixels), so size the part, not the text. A part of 380 px leaves room for one short line; with two lines, use 330 px.
- **Inline `<svg>`:** its text is scaled by displayed width ÷ viewBox width, so write the viewBox in the pixels it is shown at, e.g. `<svg viewBox="0 0 560 320" width="560" height="320">`, with `font-size` ≥ 24. Never combine `width:100%` with another viewBox width (a 600-wide viewBox shown 580 px wide turns 24 into 23.2 px). Prefer a part when one fits.

## 1. Output format

- **R-output** Reply with **exactly two fenced code blocks**, in this order, labelled `deck.html` and `narration.md` (the opening lines are ```` ```deck.html ```` and ```` ```narration.md ````). Put nothing between them; a one-line note before or after is fine. Never split a file over several blocks. Do not output files, a canvas or attachments: write both code blocks in the body of your chat message. Do not reference other files (no images, no `{{FIG:…}}`, no `{{JSON:…}}`, no external URLs, no `<link>`), and never stop in the middle of a block: if the lesson would be too long, make fewer slides (but for a range of an outline, write exactly the requested slides).
- **R-outline** When the request asks for an **outline only** (a long lesson made in two passes), reply with exactly one fenced code block labelled `outline` (the opening line is ```` ```outline ````) and no `deck.html` or `narration.md`: a Markdown table with the columns `#`, heading and point (one line), one row per slide, every slide of the lesson in order. Each later request names a range (“slides 7–12 of the outline”): write exactly those slides, following their headings and points.
- **R-noids** Do **not** write slide ids. Write `<section class="slide">` without `id`, and script headings without `{#…}`. The editor adds ids after import. When you are given a lesson that already has ids (a fix request), keep every existing `id="…"` and `{#…}` exactly as it is.

## 2. deck.html

### 2.1 Skeleton

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="default">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Lesson title</title>
</head>
<body>
<div id="stage">
  <section class="slide cover noconcl static"> … </section>
  <section class="slide"> … </section>
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

- `lang`: `en`, `ja`, … (the language of the lesson). `data-theme`: `sumi` for business and pitch decks, `kokugo` for Japanese language arts, otherwise `default`.
- No `<script>` except part data (§2.6), no `<link>`. A `<style>` block is allowed only for layout (sizes, gaps), never colors.

### 2.2 Slides

- Normal slide: `<h2>` heading, `<div class="body">…</div>`, then `<div class="concl"><span>…</span></div>` (the conclusion line: one short sentence).
- Cover: `<section class="slide cover noconcl static">` with optional `<div class="venue">…</div>`, `<h1>title</h1>`, optional `<div class="au">…</div>`.
- Chapter divider: `<section class="slide sec noconcl static"><h1>chapter title</h1></section>`.
- Classes on `<section>`: `noconcl` (no conclusion line), `static` (no steps), `nostep` (all list items visible from the start), `layout-tate` (Japanese vertical writing; only with the kokugo part set, which describes it), and the `data-morph` attribute (§2.5).
- Inside `.body`: `<p class="sub">` sub-heading, `<div class="big">` main equation, `<p class="note">` note, `<div class="thm">` theorem box, `<div class="cols">` side-by-side columns, ordinary `<p>`, `<ul>`, `<ol>`, `<table>`.
- Inline emphasis (the only way to color text): `term` (term or question), `emph` (conclusion, problem, goal), `muted` (known result, de-emphasized), `b` (bold).
- **R-headings** Every slide heading (`h1` on the cover and dividers, `h2` elsewhere) is **different** from all the others (add a word if two would be the same), and the script section of that slide starts with `## ` followed by **exactly the same heading text** (tags such as `<br>` dropped).
- **R-colors** Colors only through the theme: the classes above and the math macros `\hlE` `\hlT` `\hlM`; no hex, `rgb()`, named colors, `\color` or `\textcolor`. In a part or inline SVG: **Use only the theme's CSS variables for colors**: `var(--fg)` `var(--term)` `var(--emph)` `var(--muted)` `var(--accent2)` `var(--line)`. In SVG write `style="stroke:var(--emph)"` rather than an attribute (`DECK.el` moves `fill` and `stroke` into style automatically when they contain `var(`)

### 2.3 Steps (reveal order = speaking order)

- **R-steps** Step 0 is the slide as it first appears: context only (heading, sub-heading, one framing sentence). An element with `data-step="k"` (k = 1, 2, …) appears at step k; material (list items, equations, table rows, figure parts) appears in the order you talk about it. An equation and the sentence that introduces it share one step (wrap both in `<div data-step="k">`). About 5 steps per slide at most.
- The conclusion line automatically becomes the **last step**, `concl`; never put `data-step` on it.
- If a slide has **no** `data-step` anywhere, its top-level list items (`.body > ul > li`, `.body > ol > li`) are numbered 1, 2, … automatically. As soon as any element has `data-step`, nothing is automatic: give every revealed element its `data-step`.
- A part adds its own steps (§3), starting at its `data-from` (default 1).
- So the steps of a slide are `0 … max` plus `concl` if it has a conclusion line. A `static` slide has only step 0.

### 2.4 Math (KaTeX, rendered at build time)

- **R-math** Inline `\( … \)`, display `\[ … \]`. Write `<` as `\lt` and `>` as `\gt` inside math. Allowed macros besides standard KaTeX: `\hlE{…}` (emph) `\hlT{…}` (term) `\hlM{…}` (muted), `\htmlId{ID}{…}`, `\htmlData{mark=ID}{…}`, `\htmlClass{…}{…}`, `\morph{ID}{…}`. No `\newcommand`, no `\color`. Define each symbol where it is first used (`\(\mu\)`: the mean).

### 2.5 Attention marks and morphs

- **R-marks** The script’s `{mark:ID}` (§4) marks a target on the **same slide**. Targets: an element in the slide with `id="ID"` or `data-mark="ID"`. For part of an equation, KaTeX's `\htmlId{ID}{…}` / `\htmlData{mark=ID}{…}` (the build allows only these two and `\htmlClass`). If the same ID is used on several slides, use `data-mark` (ids must be unique in the document)
- Morph (optional): `<section class="slide" data-morph>` slides elements from the previous slide into place; pair elements with the same `data-id="…"` on both slides, or equation parts with `\morph{ID}{…}` on both. Only elements visible at step 0 move.

### 2.6 Parts

- **R-components** Animated figures are the Web Components `<m-…>` of the catalog (§3), used inside `.body`. Give each a height (`style="height:380px"`) and an `aria-label`. Data goes in **one** child `<script type="application/json">…</script>` written inline (never `{{JSON:…}}`). **Numbers in figures must be correct** (compute them; never invent values for looks; label made-up business figures as fictional). Function formulas are arithmetic expressions only (`Math.exp(x)`, `x**2`); they are never run as code. Use parts only where motion explains something; most slides need none.

### 2.7 Choosing a representation

- **R-purpose** Choose the representation from what the slide must say, not from habit. If the author names a chart type, use it. The table lists every part; use only those in the text you were given (§3, and the part sets included). If a part that is not included would fit better, say so in a one-line note.

| purpose | parts | steps |
|---|---|---|
| Compare (amounts or features) | `m-bars` (sorted for ranking), `m-compare` | One side, then the difference |
| Change over time | `m-curves`, `m-bars` (few points) | One line at a time |
| Part of a whole | `m-pie`, `m-bars` (stacked) | Whole at once |
| One key number | `m-kpi` | Whole at once |
| Steps of a process | `m-cards`, `m-flow` | One step at a time |
| Timeline, schedule | `m-timeline` | One event at a time |
| Cause and effect | `m-fishbone` | Causes, then the effect |
| Cycle | `m-cycle` | One stage at a time |
| Hierarchy, classification | `m-tree` | Top down |
| Position on 2 axes | `m-quad` | Axes, then items |
| Overlap | `m-venn` | Sets, then the overlap |
| Two quantities | `m-scatter` | Points, then the trend |
| Spread | not in this text: the nearest part, or HTML or inline SVG | Whole at once |
| Contents | `m-menu` | Whole at once |
| Predict, then check | `m-predict` | The question and choices, then the answer |
| Place / map | not in this text: the nearest part, or HTML or inline SVG | The map, then regions, points and arrows one at a time |

Some parts are not included in these instructions (for Spread, Compare (amounts or features), Steps of a process, Two quantities, Place / map, Part of a whole, Cycle, and more). Do not use them; if one would fit, say in a one-line note what you would show (the author can add parts when making a new lesson).

Each part's description (pinned version): https://github.com/egatari/components/blob/v2.7.0/components/<name>/README.md (the name without `m-`)

- **R-whole** Lists, KPI cards and pies are shown whole; do not reveal them line by line unless the script discusses each item in turn (for a list, give it one `data-step` or put `nostep` on the slide).

### 2.8 Fitting the slide (1280×720; the quality checker reports errors)

- **R-title** Heading: Japanese at most 26 units (full-width character = 1, ASCII = 0.5); English at most 60 characters. Never ends with a colon.
- **R-concl** Conclusion line: Japanese at most 35 units; English at most 70 characters. One line.
- **R-fit** The body must end above 565 px (680 px with `noconcl`): about 8 lines / 100 Japanese characters / 60 English words per slide, or one `big` equation and 3 short bullets, or a part of height ≤ 380 px and one short line (≤ 330 px with two). If it does not fit, split the slide; never shrink text and never set font sizes. Text in figures is at least 24 px.
- **R-style** Japanese slides: plain style (だ・である, 体言止め), no です・ます on slides, one punctuation style in the whole lesson (`、。` or `，．`). English slides: short phrases, sentence case.

## 3. Part catalog

These standard parts may be used in any lesson; a part set, when it is included after §6, adds the parts of its kind of material. Generated from the part READMEs (their notes are in Japanese). “steps” is how many slide steps a part uses (from `data-from`, default 1). Timing attributes (durations and delays in seconds) are not listed; their defaults fit the narration. Attribute values of type json are written as JSON in the attribute (`values="[0.1,0.5]"`). In “data shape”, `?` marks an optional field; where no type is written, label, tex, note and tone are str, step is int and at is num. In a name or label, `*…*` is italic and `_` `^` make only the next character a subscript or superscript; to show the symbol itself, write the full-width ＿ ＾ ＊.

| part | what it shows | steps | data shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<m-bars>` | Bars grow from 0 by step (vertical, horizontal, grouped, stacked); the axis max can widen by step | max group/scale step (default 1 group = 1 step) | `{groups:[{label?,value?:num,values?:num[],step?,at?,tone?} (value or values),…],series?:{label?,tone?}[],scale?:{step,max?:num,at?}[],max?:num}` |
| `<m-cards>` | Icon cards in a row or 2 rows, by step; arrows for order | largest card step (default 1 card = 1 step) | `{cards:{n?:str,icon?:str,title:str,text?:str,step?,tone?}[]}` |
| `<m-compare>` | Table comparing 2–3 things: one column, the other, then row differences | columns + 1 (diff step; none if no diff/better) | `{sides:{label,tone?,step?}[],rows:{label?,values:(str\|num)[],diff?:str,better?:int}[]}` |
| `<m-curves>` | Lines drawn one at a time on shared axes, each named at its end (no legend) | largest step (default: number of series) | `[{label?,f?:str,pts?:[num,num][],tone?,step?,labelAt?:num,color?:str,dash?:bool,xr?:[num,num],area?:any[],areaLabel?:str\|any[],at?,anchor?:"right"\|"left"\|"above"\|"below"\|"top"\|"bottom"\|"start"\|"middle"\|"end",dx?:num,dy?:num,ly?:num} (f or pts),…]` — the data is the array itself, not {"series": […]}; axes go in attributes (xr="[0,10]" xl="…"); the expression field is f in x (not fn, not u) |
| `<m-cycle>` | Cycle diagram: stage boxes on a circle clockwise from 12, joined by arc arrows (last back to first too) | number of stages (default 1 per step; per-step n each; node step wins) | `{nodes:{id?:str\|int,label?,tex?,note?,tone?,step?,at?}[],center?:{label?,tex?,note?,tone?,step?,at?},edges?:{from:str\|int,to:str\|int,label?,tone?,dash?:bool,step?,at?}[]}` |
| `<m-fishbone>` | Fishbone (cause-and-effect) diagram, one main bone at a time, head last; auto layout | bones + 1 (head), or the largest step | `{effect:{label?,tex?,note?,tone?,step?,at?},nodes:{id:str\|int,label?,tex?,note?,tone?,parent?:str\|int,step?,at?}[],edges?:{from:str\|int,to:str\|int,label?,tone?,dash?:bool,step?,at?}[]}` — nodes without parent are main bones (categories); their children are causes, grandchildren finer causes (3 levels max) |
| `<m-flow>` | Flow chart: boxes and arrows by step | largest node/edge step | `{nodes:{id:str\|int,label?,tex?,x:num,y:num,w:num,h:num,step?,tone?,at?,shape?:str}[],edges?:{from:str\|int,to:str\|int,step?,label?,tone?,dash?:bool,kind?:"money"\|"service"\|"data",amount?:str\|num,shift?:num,pulse?:bool\|any[],pulseAt?:num,offset?:num,at?,loop?:bool\|str}[]}` |
| `<m-kpi>` | KPI cards by step; count-up, change arrow, note | largest card step (default 1 card = 1 step) | `{cards:{label?,value:num,digits?:int,unit?:str,prefix?:str,from?:num,tone?,delta?:{dir?:"up"\|"down",text?:str,good?:bool},note?,step?,at?}[]}` |
| `<m-menu>` | Grid of slide-link cards (contents); plain <a href="#<slide id>">; visited mark | ceil(cards / per-step) (per-step="0": 0) | child `<a href>` links (not JSON) |
| `<m-pie>` | Pie/donut; labels inside big slices, leader lines for small | 1 (all at once); per-step n slices; or slice step | `{slices:{label?,value:num,tone?,step?,place?:"auto"\|"in"\|"out"}[],center?:str}` — the slices go in "slices" (not "data" or "groups"); value is a number, not a percentage string; the slices are drawn clockwise from 12 o'clock in the written order |
| `<m-predict>` | Predict, reveal; votes as bars, answer framed | 0 question, 1 bars, answer-step (2) | `{question?:str,choices:{label,tone?}[],answer:int,counts?:int[],note?,labels?:{correct?:str}}` — choices are objects {"label": …} (not strings); answer is the 0-based index of the right choice; counts (optional) has one whole number ≥ 0 per choice |
| `<m-quad>` | 2-axis positioning map (4 quadrants); points one per step | largest step / to.step (1 point = 1 step) | `{x?:{lo?:str,hi?:str},y?:{lo?:str,hi?:str},quads?:{tr?:str,tl?:str,bl?:str,br?:str,fill?:str},items:{label?,x:num,y:num,step?,at?,tone?,anchor?:"right"\|"left"\|"above"\|"below",r?:num,self?:bool,to?:{x:num,y:num,label?,step?,at?}}[]}` |
| `<m-scatter>` | Scatter plot; point series by step, then a trend line (least squares or 2 points) | series + trend (default 1 series = 1 step, lines 1 step) | `{series:{label?,tone?,step?,at?,points:([num,num]\|{x:num,y:num,label?,anchor?:"right"\|"left"\|"above"\|"below"\|"top"\|"bottom",tone?})[]}[],trend?:str\|{fit?:"linear",pts?:[[num,num],[num,num]],series?:int\|any[],label?,tone?,dash?:bool,step?,at?,digits?:int}\|[the same {…},…]}` — points are [x, y] or {"x", "y", "label"}; axes go in attributes (xr="[0,10]" xl="…"); trend is "linear" or {"fit": "linear", "label": "…"} or {"pts": [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]]} |
| `<m-timeline>` | Timeline; events one by one; periods as bands, overlaps stacked; end exclusive ("1912" = start of 1912) | event count (default 1 per step in time order; per-step n each; node step wins) | `{nodes:{id?:str\|int,label?,tex?,note?,tone?,when:num\|str,whenLabel?:str,end?:num\|str,lane?:str,step?,at?,after?:(str\|int)[],progress?:num}[],edges?:{from:str\|int,to:str\|int,label?,tone?,dash?:bool,step?,at?}[]}` — when / end: a number or "YYYY", "YYYY-MM", "YYYY-MM-DD"; end is exclusive ("1912" is the start of 1912). whenLabel: the date text shown instead of the computed one (when still sets the position). A node with end is a period (a band); lane groups bands into named lanes |
| `<m-tree>` | Hierarchy tree (org chart, taxonomy), built level by level from the root; auto layout | depth (by="level") or node count (by="node"); or the largest step | `{nodes:{id:str\|int,label?,tex?,note?,tone?,parent?:str\|int,branch?:str,step?,at?}[],edges?:{from:str\|int,to:str\|int,label?,tone?,dash?:bool,step?,at?}[],path?:(str\|int)[],pathStep?:int,pathNote?:str}` — exactly one node without parent (the root) |
| `<m-venn>` | Venn of 2–3 sets, one by one; then overlaps with items | sets + 1 (overlaps="each": sets + overlaps with items, or all overlaps if none) | `{sets:{label,tone?}[],regions?:{A?:str[]\|str,B?:str[]\|str,C?:str[]\|str,AB?:str[]\|str,AC?:str[]\|str,BC?:str[]\|str,ABC?:str[]\|str}}` |

### `<m-bars>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"series":[{"label":"Sales"}],"groups":[{"label":"Year 1","value":1.2},{"label":"Year 2","value":3.4}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orient` | string | `"v"` | v or h |
| `max` | number | `0` | axis max (0 = auto) |
| `unit` | string | `""` | value unit |
| `digits` | number | `0` | decimals |
| `per-step` | number | `1` | groups per step (0 = all) |
| `count` | bool | `false` | count values up |
| `ticks` | bool | `true` | ticks and grid |
| `al` | string | `""` | axis title |
| `stack` | bool | `false` | stack values; "percent" = 100 % |

For quantities shown and compared one at a time: yearly sales, ranked answers, before/after.

- group: `label` (`\n` = 2 lines), `value` or `values` (one per series), `step`, `at` (start s), `tone` (bar and value colour)
- series: `label` (2+ series: on the first group's bars; no legend), `tone` (default `--series-1..4`)
- scale: `[{"step": 3, "max": 27, "at": 0.4}]`: the max moves to `max` over `zoom` s; the old range stays as a faint band; taller bars stop at the top and grow as it widens
- `orient="h"`: names left, values right; `ticks="false"` for ranks
- `stack="true"` (`"percent"` = 100 %): a group's `values` in one bar; total at the end, values inside segments; values ≥ 0

Notes

- Values appear once a bar is fully grown; `count="true"` counts them up
- Series names sit on the first group's bars: keep to 2–3 series

### `<m-cards>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"cards":[{"icon":"user","title":"Listen","text":"Hear the problem"},{"icon":"bulb","title":"Think","text":"Find 3 ideas"},{"icon":"rocket","title":"Try","text":"Build small, show"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layout` | enum | `"row"` | row, or grid (2×2; 3×2 for 5–6) |
| `arrows` | bool | `false` | order arrows (grid: Z order) |
| `nums` | bool | `false` | number circles |
| `hilite` | string | `""` | last or a number (from 1) |
| `per-step` | number | `1` | cards per step (0 = all) |

3–4 short equal points or a 2×2: try cards over bullets; short steps: cards with arrows. Long or unequal items: bullets.

(2–6 cards).

- `title`: required, ≤ 2 lines. `text`: wraps; overflow cut with …, reported
- `icon`: Tabler name (below); unknown = dashed box, reported
- `n`: circle text (`"A"`, `"1"`); `nums` numbers the rest 1, 2, 3 …
- `tone`: circle and icon colour (`term`, `emph`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`)
- `arrows`; `hilite="last"` or `"3"`: `--emph` frame and fill
- `variant`: `rise` (default), `fade`, `draw`

Icons:

- People: user users user-check user-plus user-circle friends mood-smile man woman id-badge
- Data: chart-bar chart-line chart-pie chart-dots trending-up trending-down table database filter adjustments percentage sum
- Money: coin cash credit-card wallet receipt pig-money building-bank report-money shopping-cart tag
- Time: clock calendar calendar-event calendar-time hourglass history alarm stopwatch
- Place: map-pin map world home building building-factory building-store route truck
- Flow: arrow-right arrows-right-left refresh repeat circle-check checklist list-numbers git-branch target flag rocket hand-click
- Talk: message messages mail phone bell speakerphone share world-www microphone presentation
- Docs: file file-text files notebook book clipboard-list folder news certificate award
- Tools: tool settings hammer bulb puzzle cpu device-laptop device-mobile robot code scale
- Nature: leaf tree plant sun moon cloud cloud-rain droplet flame snowflake
- Safety: shield shield-check lock key alert-triangle first-aid-kit heart heart-rate-monitor eye
- Learning: school pencil ruler math-function atom flask microscope palette music language

### `<m-compare>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"sides":[{"label":"Paper form","tone":"muted"},{"label":"Online form"}],"rows":[{"label":"Hours","values":["Weekdays 9–17","24 h"],"better":1,"diff":"Any time"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | number | `28` | value text px (shrinks to 24) |
| `diff-label` | string | `""` | diff column heading |

2–3 things on the same points (old vs new, A vs B). Bars: `m-bars`; one number: `m-kpi`.

- `sides`: 2 or 3; `label` = column heading; `tone` (`term`, `emph`, `muted`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`; default `term`, `accent2`, `series-4`); `muted` = old
- `rows`: `label` = point (optional); `values` in column order (text/number; `\n`), count = `sides` (else error card)
- `diff`: short difference, `--emph`, right column
- `better`: better column index (from 0): bold, `--emph` frame at diff step
- Steps: column 1 (+ point names) → 2 → (3) → diffs; column `step` overrides
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `slide`, `reveal` (row by row); same steps

### `<m-curves>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `[{"label":"Demand D","f":"10 - x"},{"label":"Supply S","f":"2 + x"},{"label":"Equilibrium","pts":[[4,0],[4,6]],"dash":true}]`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xr` | json | `[0, 1]` | x range |
| `yr` | json | `[0, 1]` | y range |
| `xt` | json | `[]` | x ticks |
| `yt` | json | `[]` | y ticks |
| `xf` | number |  | x tick decimals |
| `yf` | number |  | y tick decimals |
| `xl` | string | `""` | x title |
| `yl` | string | `""` | y title |
| `n` | number | `300` | samples |
| `lw` | number | `3.5` | line width |
| `size` | number | `0` | text px (≥ 24; 0 = default) |

One comparison at a time: mean, median, quantiles; losses.

Series: a JSON array in a child script. One series = one step; same `step` = together.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `label` | line name |
| `f` | expression in x (see below) |
| `pts` | points `[[x, y], …]` |
| `tone` | `term` `emph` `accent2` `muted` `fg` `series-1..4` |
| `dash` | dashed |
| `area` / `areaLabel` | shaded span `[a, b]` (several; null = edge), labels |
| `labelAt` / `anchor` / `dx` / `dy` / `ly` | name at x = `labelAt` (default: end); `anchor` `right` `left` `above` `below`; `ly` = y |

`f` is arithmetic, not code: numbers, `x`, `Math` functions/constants (`sin(x)`, `PI`; no `random`), `N(x, mean, sd)`, `+ - * / % **`, comparisons, `&& || !`, `? :`. Powers: `**`. An unreadable `f` shows a card.

### `<m-cycle>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"center":{"label":"PDCA"},"nodes":[{"label":"Plan"},{"label":"Do"},{"label":"Check"},{"label":"Act"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `per-step` | number | `1` | stages per step (0 = all) |
| `size` | number | `26` | box text px (shrinks to 24) |

Stages that repeat in order: PDCA, water cycle, cell cycle. No coordinates; list stages in order (conventions §2).

(`center`, `edges` optional).

- `nodes`: stages (3–8), in order clockwise from 12; arcs to the next, last→first automatic
  - `label` (`\n`) or `tex` (KaTeX), `note` (small 2nd line, `--muted`), `tone` (`term` default, `emph`, `muted`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`), `step`, `at`, `id`
- `center`: middle name, an object (`{"label": "PDCA", "note": "…"}`); appears with stage 1 (`center.step`). `m-pie`'s `center` is a string
  - same fields as nodes, no `id`; `tone: emph` box: `--emph-tint` fill, `--emph` frame/text
- `edges`: extra links (`from` `to` = node `id`s, `label` `tone` `dash` `step`); dashed arrows edge to edge
- Arrows `--muted`, 3 px

Layout:

- Wide spaces: ellipse up to 1.9× wider (never taller); sized to fit the element
- Incoming arrow appears with its box; last→first after the last box
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `draw` (arrows first), `grow`; same steps and end
- `cues(k)`: start times of 2nd+ boxes in one step

### `<m-fishbone>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"effect":{"label":"Late delivery"},"nodes":[{"id":"p","label":"People"},{"id":"p1","label":"Short-staffed","parent":"p"},{"id":"m","label":"Machines"},{"id":"m1","label":"Truck breakdown","parent":"m"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | string | `"causes-first"` | causes-first (default) or effect-first |
| `size` | number | `0` | box text px (0 = 27, shrink to 24) |

Grouped causes of one effect (e.g. 4M: people, machines, methods, materials). No coordinates.

(`edges` optional).

- effect (head): `label` (`\n`) or `tex`, `note` (under box), `tone` (default `emph`), `step`, `at`
- node: `id`, `label` (or `tex`), `note`, `parent`, `tone`, `step`, `at`. No `parent` = main bone; child = cause; grandchild = sub-cause (3 levels)
  - Bones in array order, left to right, top/bottom alternating; name boxed at the outer end (`note` outside)
  - Cause `tex` = KaTeX; `note` small after the name (`--muted`)
  - `tone`: bone = box and bone; cause = text and line (`emph` bold)
- edge: extra cause links (`from` `to` `label` `tone` `dash` `step`), dashed arrow bulging left of text; best within one bone
- `order`: `causes-first` or `effect-first` (head, spine first); node `step` wins
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `draw` (lines first), `grow` (boxes grow in); moves ≤ 12 px
- Fit (1280×720 body, ~440 px high): ≤ 3 rows (causes + sub-causes) per bone (4 if short), 4–6 bones, causes ≤ ~10 chars. Text ≥ 24 px; overflow spills and is reported. Too many: split or shorten

|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | number | `26` | box text px |
| `pulse-n` | number | `3` | pulse dots |
| `label-gap` | number | `12` | min label–box gap px |

; px; `x`, `y` = box top-left, `w`, `h` = size.

- node: `id`, `label` (`\n`) or `tex` (KaTeX), `step`, `tone` (`term`/`emph`/`muted`), `at` (start s), `shape:"diamond"` (decision; ~2× text width)
- edge: `from` `to` `step` (default: later end), `label`, `tone`, `dash`, `offset` (label gap), `at`, `loop` (back edge: `"left"` `"right"` `"top"` `"bottom"` or `true` = auto)

### `<m-kpi>`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cols` | number | `0` | cards per row (0 = count, ≤ 4) |
| `digits` | number | `0` | decimals (card wins) |
| `per-step` | number | `1` | cards per step (0 = all) |
| `count` | bool | `true` | count up |
| `size` | number | `0` | number px (0 = auto) |

- `label`: above. `value` (`digits`, commas). `unit`: after. `prefix`: before (`+`, `~`). Negative `value` has its own −: no `prefix` `−` (−−12); `prefix: "−"` only with a positive decrease
- `from`: count start (default 0; may count down)
- `tone`: number, top band (`term`, `emph`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`)
- `delta`: `{"dir": "up" | "down", "text": "+4", "good": true}`: ▲/▼ + text; good (default `up`) `--term`, bad `--emph`
- `note`: bottom line
- `variant`: `count` (default), `rise`, `flip`, `underline`; `count="false"` → `rise`
- `cues(k)`: start times of 2nd+ cards in a step (for `{cue}`)

### `<m-menu>`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cols` | number | `0` | columns (0 = auto) |
| `per-step` | number | `0` | cards per step (0 = all, no steps) |
| `size` | number | `34` | title px |
| `visited` | bool | `true` | mark visited cards |

Contents; choosing where to start. Add the menu after import; in the first draft use a plain list.
```html
<m-menu cols="3" aria-label="Today">
  <a href="#s-njd4kp" data-icon="1" data-sub="Poet">Poem A</a>
  <a href="#s-uhqygr:2" data-icon="2" data-sub="Order">Poem B</a>
</m-menu>
```

- One child `<a href>` = one card. `href`: `#<slide id>` (step 0) or `#<id>:<step>` (`0`, `1`, … `concl`); ids are added on import; content = title
- `data-icon`: circle text (`1`, `A`). `data-sub`: subtitle
- `per-step="n"`: n cards per step (from `data-from`); unshown cards inert. `0` = all at once
- `cols` default: ≤ 3 cards 1 row, 4 → 2, more → 3. Min height `--mm-h` (104px), gap `--mm-gap` (18px). Fill, centred: `style="height:100%;align-content:center;--mm-h:150px"`

### `<m-pie>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"slices":[{"label":"Food","value":7.2},{"label":"Housing","value":8.5},{"label":"Other","value":2.1,"tone":"muted"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `donut` | number | `0` | inner radius ratio (0 = pie) |
| `unit` | string | `""` | value unit |
| `digits` | number | `0` | value decimals |
| `pct-digits` | number | `0` | percent decimals |
| `show` | string | `"pct"` | pct, value, both or none |
| `per-step` | number | `0` | slices per step (0 = all) |

Shares of a whole, all at once. Fine comparison: `m-bars`.

- slice: `label`, `value` (percent computed), `tone` (`term` `emph` `accent2` `muted` `fg` `series-1..4`), `step`, `place` (`auto` default, `in`, `out`)
  - Clockwise from 12 in order; "Other" last, `"tone": "muted"`
  - ≤ 6–7 slices
- `center`: hole text, a string (`\n`; `{total}` = sum, e.g. `"Answers\n{total}"`); `m-cycle`'s `center` is an object
- `donut`: `0.5`–`0.6`
- `show` (under name): `pct` (default), `value`, `both`, `none`
- `unit` `digits`: value unit, decimals; `pct-digits` (default 0). Percents rounded to sum to 100%
- Steps: all at step 1; `per-step="1"` only if narrated slice by slice (outline faint). Slice `step` wins
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `sweep` (clockwise from 12), `grow` (rim grows out)

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"question":"Which falls first?","choices":[{"label":"Heavy"},{"label":"Light"},{"label":"Same"}],"answer":2,"counts":[14,3,9],"note":"No air: same"}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|

### `<m-quad>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"x":{"lo":"Manual","hi":"Auto"},"y":{"lo":"Costly","hi":"Cheap"},"items":[{"label":"Co. A","x":0.25,"y":0.7},{"label":"Us","x":0.8,"y":0.82,"self":true}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | number | `26` | label px |
| `quads-step` | number | `0` | quadrant-name step (0 = start) |

Positioning, effect×effort, SWOT: show the empty space.

- `x` `y`: axis end words (step 0)
- `quads`: names (tr = top-right, tl, bl, br); `fill: "tr"` tints one; names at `quads-step`
- item: `label`, `x` `y` (0–1; 0.5 = axis cross), `step` (default next), `at`, `tone` (`term`/`fg`; default muted), `anchor` (`right`, `left`, `above`, `below`), `r`

- `to: {"x", "y", "label", "step", "at"}`: slides at `to.step` (default next), dashed trail; `label` on arrival

### `<m-scatter>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"series":[{"label":"Sunny","points":[[24,210],[28,380],[31,560],{"x":34,"y":690,"label":"Heatwave"}]}],"trend":"linear"}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xr` | json | `null` | x range |
| `yr` | json | `null` | y range |
| `xt` | json | `null` | x ticks |
| `yt` | json | `null` | y ticks |
| `xf` | number |  | x tick decimals |
| `yf` | number |  | y tick decimals |
| `xl` | string | `""` | x title |
| `yl` | string | `""` | y title |
| `r` | number | `9` | point radius px |

Relation of two quantities (heat vs sales). Points, then trend.

- series: `points` (`[x, y]` or `{"x", "y", "label", "anchor", "tone"}`), `label` (series name, top with marker), `tone` (`term` `emph` `accent2` `muted` `fg` `series-1..4`), `step` (1 series = 1 step; same = together), `at` (start s)
  - Point `label` placed clear of overlaps (`anchor` = first try: `right` `left` `above` `below`); outliers only
  - Marker shape per series; repeats after 4, so ≤ 4 series
- trend: `"linear"` (least squares on all points), or `{"fit": "linear", "series": 0, "label", "tone", "dash", "step", "at", "digits"}`, or `{"pts": [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]]}` (segment; exactly 2 points; vertical OK); several = array
  - `series`: fitted series index from 0, or array (default all)
  - `label`: `{r}` correlation, `{a}` slope, `{b}` intercept (`digits`, default 2), e.g. `"Trend (r = {r})"`
  - `step`: default after the last series
  - Clipped to the plot; lines outside reported. Vertical `pts`: `{a}` `{b}` empty; `{r}` only for fits
- Axes: `xr` `yr` range, `xt` `yt` ticks, `xf` `yf` decimals, `xl` `yl` titles; range/ticks auto if omitted
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `sweep` (left to right), `grow` (points grow, line from the middle)
- Show later steps faintly (`ctx.preview`): later points and lines faint

### `<m-timeline>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"nodes":[{"id":"a","label":"Meiji Restoration","when":"1868","whenLabel":"Meiji 1"},{"id":"b","label":"Constitution","when":"1889","note":"Feb 11"},{"id":"c","label":"Sino-Japanese War","when":"1894","end":"1895","tone":"emph"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orient` | string | `"h"` | h or v |
| `scale` | string | `"time"` | time or even |
| `per-step` | number | `1` | events per step (0 = all) |
| `size` | number | `26` | label px (shrinks to 24) |
| `unit` | string | `""` | ticks: day, week, month |
| `today` | string | `""` | today line (YYYY-MM-DD) |

History, lives, schedules. No coordinates; content and times only.

(`edges` optional).

- `when`: number (`1868`, `-500`, `0.5`) or `"YYYY"` `"YYYY-MM"` `"YYYY-MM-DD"`; shown as the date line
- `whenLabel`: text replacing the date ("Meiji 1"); `when` still sets position
- `label` (`\n`) or `tex` (KaTeX)
- `note`: small last line in the box (`--muted`); after the name for periods/milestones
- `tone`: `term` (default), `emph`, `muted`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`
- `end`: period, a band below the axis; name inside (or beside); `\n` names thicken it
- `end` is exclusive: Meiji 1868–1912 and Taishō 1912–1926 share a row; through December = next month (`"2027-01"`)
- `lane`: named group of rows ("Eras", "Authors"); overlaps stack within; `lane` without `end` = milestone (◆)
- `step`, `at` (start s)
- `edges`: extra links (`from` `to` `label` `tone` `dash` `step`); dashed arrows (`dash: false` solid)
- Schedules: `after: ["id", …]` (arrow end→start), `progress` (0–100 %); `today` line; tick `unit`
  - `after` only between periods and milestones; `today` needs a period

Layout:

- `orient`: `h` (default) or `v`; `scale`: `time` (default) or `even` (very uneven gaps)
- Events (no `end` or `lane`): axis dot plus date-and-name box, alternating sides (`v`: left/right); 2 rows when crowded
- With periods: round ticks; event boxes all above the axis
- Steps: time order, periods and events together; the axis comes with the first
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `draw` (lines first, bands drawn), `grow` (boxes grow, bands stretch); same steps and end
- Show later steps faintly (`ctx.preview`): later items faint
- `cues(k)`: start times of 2nd+ items in a step (for `{cue}`)

### `<m-tree>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"nodes":[{"id":"r","label":"Animals"},{"id":"a","label":"Vertebrates","parent":"r"},{"id":"b","label":"Invertebrates","parent":"r"}]}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orient` | string | `"down"` | down (default) or right |
| `by` | string | `"level"` | level (default) or node (depth-first) |
| `link` | string | `"elbow"` | elbow (default) or straight |
| `size` | number | `0` | box text px (0 = 27, shrink to 24) |

Parent–child structures (org charts, taxonomies, outlines). No coordinates; laid out without overlaps.

(`edges` optional).

- node: `id`, `label` (`\n`) or `tex` (KaTeX), `parent` (parent `id`; exactly one root without `parent`), `note` (small, **under** box), `tone` (`term` default, `emph`, `muted`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`), `step`, `at` (start s)
- Children in array order; parent centred over them
- edge: extra links (`from` `to` `label` `tone` `dash` `step`), dashed arrow outside the tree; best at same depth; step: later end
- Child `branch`: line text (e.g. probability). `path`: root-first `id`s highlighted in turn (default 1 step per line, after the tree; `pathStep`: in one step; `pathNote`: end note)
- `orient="right"` for wide taxonomies. `by="node"`: one at a time, depth-first (to follow a branch). Node `step` wins
- Lines `--muted`, 3 px; `tone: emph` box: `--emph-tint` fill
- Fit (~440 px high): ~8 four-character boxes per level (`down`), ~7 (`right`); ~5 levels. More leaves: 2 staggered rows (~16 / ~11), then 2-line names. Text ≥ 24 px; overflow spills, reported. Too many: split
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `draw` (lines first), `grow`
- Show later steps faintly (`ctx.preview`): later parts faint

### `<m-venn>`

Data example (child `<script type="application/json">`): `{"sets":[{"label":"Mammals"},{"label":"Sea animals"}],"regions":{"A":["Lion"],"B":["Tuna"],"AB":["Whale","Dolphin"]}}`

| prop | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | number | `26` | item text px (shrinks to 24) |
| `spread` | number | `1` | centre distance ÷ radius (0.7–1.3) |
| `overlaps` | string | `"together"` | together or each |

Shared and distinct traits. Per-point values: `m-compare`.

- `sets`: 2 or 3; `label` outside; `tone` (`term`, `emph`, `muted`, `accent2`, `series-1..4`; default `term`, `accent2`, `series-4`). Avoid `emph` (used for overlaps)
- `regions`: items per region (array or `\n` text). Keys: letters in alphabetical order, A B C = `sets` order:
  - `A`: only A; `AB`: A and B (with 3 sets, not C); `ABC`: all three
  - 2 sets: `A` `B` `AB`; 3: `A` `B` `C` `AB` `AC` `BC` `ABC`; all optional. C keys with 2 sets: error card
- Area not to scale. `spread` (default 1): smaller = more overlap
- Overlap items bold; 1–2 words with 3 sets
- Steps: each set with its own items → overlaps (those with items tinted `--emph`, outlined, items shown; if none have items, all). `overlaps="each"`: one by one (`AB`, `AC`, `BC`, `ABC`)
- `variant`: `fade` (default), `draw` (outlines first)

## 4. narration.md

```markdown
# Script: <lesson title>

## The decay law
[0] Here is the decay law. We follow how many atoms are left.
[1] The number left is the starting number times a shrinking exponential.
[2] {mark:n0|circle}{N₀|N naught} is the number at the start, at time zero.
[concl] The half-life depends only on the decay constant.
```

- One section per slide, **in slide order, for every slide (cover included)**: `## <slide heading>` (R-headings), no `{#id}` (R-noids).
- **R-narr-steps** Step labels `[0]`, `[1]`, … and `[concl]`. **Every step of every slide has script lines** (step 0 to max, and `[concl]` if the slide has a conclusion line), and there are **no labels for steps that do not exist** (a `static` cover has only `[0]`; a slide without a conclusion line has no `[concl]`; never `[01]`). Within a step, talk only about what appears at that step.
- **R-dialogue** **One narrator by default**: write no speaker names. Write a dialogue only when asked (if asked for three or more speakers, keep two roles and say so first): lines start with `Expert:` or `Novice:` (continuation lines indented; a line without a speaker is Expert), shaped as a cognitive apprenticeship:
  - Novice is never a mere backchannel: Novice voices the question a learner is likely to have, or paraphrases (“So …, is that right?”)
  - Expert answers and adds one example or analogy, or confirms (or corrects) the paraphrase and takes one step further
  - Only at a comprehension fork (where learners tend to misunderstand, or a “why” remains): at most one exchange per slide, 2–3 turns. Elsewhere Expert alone
  - Never a turn that is only “I see”, or that repeats the previous turn. Example: `Novice: So a larger rate always gets there faster?` `Expert: Not always. Too large, and each step jumps across the valley, like striding downhill onto the opposite slope.`
- `{note:…}`: presenter directions.
- `{cue}`: a sync point inside a step, one per entry of the part’s `cues(k)` (only where a part’s README asks for it; otherwise omit).
- `{mark:ID}`, `{mark:ID|effect}`, `{mark:ID|effect|hold=seconds}`, `{mark:clear}`: placed **right before** the words about the target; at most 1–2 per step; still say the thing in words. Effects: `underline` (default; a hand-drawn underline from left to right), `circle` (a hand-drawn circle), `box` (a rounded frame), `spot` (dims everything except the area around the target with the background color), `laser` (a dot of light slides to below the target and stays briefly)
- **R-reading** `{display|reading}` gives the reading of **one symbol or one term**: `{θ|theta}`, `{N₀|N naught}`, `{x̄|x bar}`, `{論語|ろんご}`. One symbol may carry a star, a prime, a subscript or superscript, or a hat/bar/tilde (`{Q*|Q star}`, `{x′|x prime}`, `{θ̂|theta hat}`). Write the display part in plain Unicode, not LaTeX, and never as an expression or several symbols (`{1-η|…}`, `{a*b|…}` and `{θとη|…}` are wrong: give each symbol its own reading and say the relation in words).
- **R-formula** **Never read an equation aloud**: no LaTeX, no `\`, `^`, `_`, and no strings such as `a + b = c` in the narration. Say what the equation means (“the number left is the starting number times a shrinking exponential”).
- Japanese script is polite spoken Japanese (です・ます); English script is plain spoken English. About 5 Japanese characters or 2.5 English words per second; 1–3 sentences per turn.

## 5. Fix requests

When the user pastes a **fix request** (a list of findings with the ids of the standards, followed by the current files), fix exactly those findings, keep everything else, keep every `id="…"` and `{#…}` unchanged (R-noids), and reply again with the two blocks (R-output). If the request contains only some slides, return only those `<section>` elements in the `deck.html` block (no `<html>`) and only their sections in the `narration.md` block; the editor puts them back in place by id.

## 6. Worked example

A small lesson, fictional, showing the structure only (do not copy its content). Note how the steps add up: the list of 2 items gives steps 1–2 and `[concl]`; the `m-flow` with 4 boxes gives steps 1–4. The static cover has `[0]` only. Some part sets end with an example of their own.

### Common (English, default theme, marks, m-flow)

```deck.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="default">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>How a web page arrives</title>
</head>
<body>
<div id="stage">

<section class="slide cover noconcl static">
  <div class="venue">Computing basics, lesson 1 (a fictional course)</div>
  <h1>How a web page arrives</h1>
</section>

<section class="slide">
  <h2>Two programs take part</h2>
  <div class="body">
    <p>Opening a page is a conversation between two programs.</p>
    <ul>
      <li id="browser">The <span class="term">browser</span> asks for the page and draws it</li>
      <li id="server">The <span class="term">server</span> keeps the page and sends it back</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="concl"><span>Every page load is a request and a reply</span></div>
</section>

<section class="slide">
  <h2>From the address to the screen</h2>
  <div class="body">
    <m-flow style="height:300px" aria-label="Four stages: type the address, send a request, send the page back, draw the page">
      <script type="application/json">{"nodes": [
        {"id": "a", "label": "Type the\naddress", "x": 10, "y": 100, "w": 250, "h": 110, "step": 1},
        {"id": "b", "label": "Send a\nrequest", "x": 315, "y": 100, "w": 250, "h": 110, "step": 2},
        {"id": "c", "label": "Send the\npage back", "x": 620, "y": 100, "w": 250, "h": 110, "step": 3, "tone": "term"},
        {"id": "d", "label": "Draw the\npage", "x": 925, "y": 100, "w": 250, "h": 110, "step": 4, "tone": "emph"}
      ], "edges": [
        {"from": "a", "to": "b"}, {"from": "b", "to": "c"}, {"from": "c", "to": "d"}
      ]}</script>
    </m-flow>
  </div>
  <div class="concl"><span>A slow page is slow in one of these four stages</span></div>
</section>

</div>
</body>
```

```narration.md
# Narration: How a web page arrives

## How a web page arrives
[0] Today we follow a web page on its way from a server to your screen.

## Two programs take part
[0] Opening a page is a conversation between two programs.
[1] {mark:browser}The browser is the program you look at. It asks for the page and then draws it.
[2] {mark:server}The server is a program on another computer. It keeps the page and sends it back when asked.
[concl] Every page load is a request and a reply.

## From the address to the screen
[0] Let us put the steps in order.
[1] First you type the address of the page.
[2] The browser turns it into a request and sends it to the server.
[3] The server finds the page and sends it back.
[4] The browser draws the page on the screen.
[concl] When a page is slow, one of these four stages is taking the time.
```
